name: Cloxacillin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Cloxacillin is a short-acting antistaphylococcal penicillin, 94% protein-bound, with 37% of an oral dose excreted in urine. The Canadian product monograph gives no kidney dose adjustment (half-life about 25 minutes, 49 minutes in uremia) but warns that high levels in kidney failure can cause central nervous system toxicity. It has no current US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: The Canadian product monograph does not grade kidney impairment; bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Usual: 250 to 500 mg orally every 6 hours, 1 to 2 hours before meals; maximum 6,000 mg/day (PM).

hd: No dialysis data in the PM. Highly protein-bound (94%), so removal is likely small; avoid the highest doses. Specialist input.
monitoring: Kidney, liver and blood counts periodically in long courses; neurotoxicity (myoclonus, seizures) at high levels in kidney failure; severe skin reactions (PM).

pediatric.approved_ages: Pediatric doses not given in this product monograph; limited experience in premature and newborn infants (use with caution).
